correctness.rationale: After time change tau=log h(t), bounded growth becomes exponential. Uniform noncriticality at r-C bounds each bounded future orbit on [s+C,infinity) by theta times its total supremum; hence supremum occurs in the initial C-window, giving M<=K exp(omega C)||v|| and making every stable bounded-orbit subspace S(s) closed. Cocycle and finite-time boundedness imply S(0)=T(s,0)^(-1)S(s). Choose a d-dimensional complement Z to closed S(0). Then T(s,0)Z is d-dimensional and transverse to S(s); T(s,0)X lies in S(s)+T(s,0)Z, which is closed. Dense range yields X=S(s) directsum T(s,0)Z, so codim S(s)=d at every time. This supplies exactly the missing hypothesis for Dragičević Theorem 3; its other implications close the equivalence cycle. Independent operator analysis of T(t,s)=diag((h(s)/h(t))^n,(h(t)/h(s))) on ell^2(N) plus R confirms dense non-surjective positive-time ranges, invariant stable codim1 and dichotomy. No finite simulation is used as a general functional-analytic proof.

originality.rationale: The primary Dragičević arXiv:2611.08451 theorem requires finite stable codimension at every s, and Example 1 demonstrates initial-only codimension fails for some noninvertible evolutions. The new dense-range assumption is a precise sufficient regularity condition, not present in the theorem, making the all-time assumption automatic while allowing non-surjective smoothing evolutions. The proof is a short functional-analytic bridge, but its applicability is mathematically motivated and not mechanically a restatement.
